pages.title: Eating Raw Food
pages.text:
Eating raw meat and other uncooked foods $(#e05252)isn't free$(). Nourished tracks what you eat and penalizes you when you skip the campfire.

The penalty scales with how raw the food is — there are three tiers: $(bold)Mild$(), $(bold)Medium$(), and $(bold)Severe$().

pages.title: Mild
pages.text:
$(#E8C24F)Mild$() penalties apply to foods that are technically edible raw but clearly not ideal — lightly processed or borderline items.

You take a small nutrient penalty and miss out on a portion of the nutrition the cooked version would have given. Not a disaster, but it adds up.

pages.title: Medium
pages.text:
$(#e05252)Medium$() penalties apply to clearly raw foods — standard raw meats like beef, pork, and chicken.

The nutrient penalty is larger and a significant portion of the nutrition is lost compared to eating the cooked version. You are also more likely to trigger gut flora damage at this tier.

pages.title: Severe
pages.text:
$(#e05252)Severe$() penalties apply to foods that should never be eaten raw under any circumstances.

Nutrient bars take a meaningful hit, nearly all of the cooked nutrition is denied, and your gut flora takes the hardest damage. Just cook it.

pages.title: Missed Opportunity
pages.text:
Every tier includes a $(bold)missed opportunity$() multiplier. This is the fraction of nutrition the cooked version would have given that you simply don't get.

Eating raw doesn't just hurt you — it wastes the food. A raw beef gives far less Protein than a cooked one, even before the penalty kicks in.

pages.title: Memory
pages.text:
Nourished remembers recent raw food events for a short window. If you eat something raw and then eat the same thing cooked shortly after, the system won't reroll the penalty.

This prevents the system from double-punishing you during the same eating session.
